text: At the same time, because of the diversity inherent in this Tapestry, texturally we can be a little rough at times.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There will be rough and tough times when some threads in the Tapestry wonder why they are in this Tapestry, or why other threads are in the Tapestry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And these questions do not just revolve just around questions of race and religion, but to newer, perhaps more divisive and contentious issues, including questions concerning LGBT, equality, personal freedoms.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: How then do we weave the Singapore Tapestry tightly, but at the same time, ensuring enough space in between the different threads for diversity to exist harmoniously?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is quite a paradox, but it is a paradox that we must, and we can and we have to overcome.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Race is one of the primary threads of our social fabric, and the fact that different races are acknowledged while also bound by a shared belonging is what make our Tapestry strong, cohesive and also highly unique.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is an ideal that we have been striving towards for more than 55 years, since we started our little nation – the day we became independent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On Separation Day itself, Mr Lee Kuan Yew affirmed that Singapore is "not a Malay nation, not a Chinese nation, not an Indian nation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Everybody will have a place in Singapore", and that is how we started.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And after decades of nation-building, we are today less race- conscious and more tolerant of each other.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: More "one united people, regardless of race, language or religion".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The young especially, are closer to this ideal than perhaps, their parents and grandparents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we must also ask ourselves, how did we get here?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There was certainly nothing natural or expected in the progression from Singapore to Singaporean, as the tagline for the Singapore Bicentennial last year put it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If it were indeed an expected natural trajectory, or a natural progression, it would have occurred elsewhere in the world naturally, including among our neighbours in ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We got here precisely because we have worked hard at it consistently and systematically, through policies that touch almost every aspect of our lives.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We live together, our children play together, they study together, and our sons do the National Service together.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We recognise that communities can be narrow and exclusive, as well as generous and inclusive, and our policies must be aimed to promote the latter and counter the former.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Common spaces like our public parks, schools, libraries, sports facilities, and public housing where all races interact, deliberately and accidentally, help to promote a more open and	shared outlook across communities by creating opportunities for social mixing and simply doing things together.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is absolutely nothing natural or inevitable about any of this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It did not happen by itself, and it is not something which will endure by itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We must not think that we have arrived or that we have reached an ideal post-racial state that has been attained and that no further more effort by way of these policies need to be put in place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Race and religion remain faultlines and they remain highly emotive issues.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the risk of regressing on what we have achieved is always there.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we cannot assume that our progress will be a straight line.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In Singapore, consciousness of race cannot be erased – nor should it be.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Indeed, if we were all the same, we would have nothing unique to contribute, nor learn from anyone else.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because we are not the same, we each have something unique to contribute, to bring to the table, something only we can give to the common good of all of us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The more diverse we are, the richer our culture becomes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We should view difference from the lens of contribution, and not separation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nor should being "one united people, regardless of race" mean that we should renounce our cultural affinities or discourage people of the same community from coming together to support each other, and others in the community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The affinities of race have been harnessed to foster a spirit of self-help among our communities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, Vibrance @ Yishun organises programs to serve all ethnic groups, even while it conducts its own programmes specifically to meet the needs of respective communities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: SHGs may be race-based, but they are far from race-bound.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And not only are the beneficiaries of these gropus across racial lines – so are the volunteers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our ideal is that one day, we want to see a Singapore, where we do not need such SHGs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But that is not going to come about by wishing the differences away.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It can only come about by working at it actively, daily and consciously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And on critical issues such as education, economic upliftment, beyond the main efforts by the Government, the communities and SHGs are mobilised, ground up with their own initiatives to help people, help community, and this must be welcomed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our diversity and geography means that we must always be conscious and do what we can to sustain our multiracial society.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are not starting from a blank slate, but we cannot take the peace we enjoy for granted, nor can we take our social fabric, built up over generations, for granted.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we must recognise that it takes years to weave a good Tapestry, but mere moments to destroy it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And once the threads start unravelling, it will be difficult to bridge the social divide, the racial divide, the ethnic divide and to stitch the Tapestry back together, will be a mammoth task.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I believe our youths must have as much a voice in this discourse as anyone else.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On issues of race and other aspects of our Tapestry, not only between youths themselves, but across generations, with other people.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We need to talk about how we can refresh and revitalise the bonds that bind us, because the social solidarity that we enjoy today, that we sometimes take for granted today, has proven so important, especially in today's pandemic and the crisis.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The ructions and the affray that bedevil a migrant society such as the United States is constant a reminder that inclusiveness will always be a work in progress for us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Nor are older societies, like Germany, where an anti-lockdown movement is emerging, immune from divisions and distrust that cause society to fracture under stress.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When society is torn apart by xenophobia and prejudices that appeal not to our better self, but to our worst instincts, it becomes impossible to even talk about a caring society.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And that must be something we always keep at the back of our minds as we build a nation for tomorrow, as we build a more inclusive and caring society.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: How do we apply all of this to the desire to build a more inclusive society?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It means a few things, starting with having to practise and work on inclusiveness every day.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We must acknowledge our differences and accept that despite these differences, we live peacefully together, happily because we are in the same boat, in the same place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I should add that inclusiveness is not about ignoring or just living with differences or denying that different groups have different or even conflicting agendas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is about accepting that there is always going to be some give and take, and appreciating that everyone is entitled to their own positions as long as those positions do not encroach on another group's right to also have a position, albeit a different one, and perhaps even one that you might disagree with.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Inclusiveness is about acceptance and appreciation and not about changing others to something in your own image.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This requires a certain maturity of thought in order for a meaningful discourse to take place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It also requires common values that anchor the social compact between Singaporeans as well as between the Government and the people.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Singapore Tapestry that I spoke of can magically enlarge the space that we share beyond the physical limitations of our small, tiny city-state island, and it mysteriously also deepens the roots of our young country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It exists beyond the realms of material goods, physical infrastructure and GDP growth.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so I return to the discussion on the pillars of MCCY.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The four pillars of MCCY may be more software than hardware but they play a big part in holding the Singapore Tapestry together.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Sports, arts, culture and a shared heritage are the avenues which help connect people and lead us to a better understanding of ourselves and of who and where we are in our community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this vein, MCCY will play a part in this journey of deepening our roots and increasing our common spaces so that a more inclusive and caring Singapore will come into being.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our security framework ensures our political existence as a nation while our economic activity supports our physical prosperity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These two are critical but are in themselves insufficient for our long-term survival as a sovereign and thriving city state.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is always that something more, something abstract that makes our nation great.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To our youths, I want to say this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And one day, you can look back and tell your own kids of how mom and dad overcame the crisis of a generation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By uniting with fellow Singaporeans and by leaving behind a more beautiful and tightly knitted Tapestry as a legacy for generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, to clarify my own speech, which he referred to.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Certainly, I do not take our multiracialism for granted.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In fact, in my speech, I did acknowledge that it is a difficult task that the Government has to foster a Singapore identity in a heterogeneous population and I do not take anything away from the Government's concerns.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think I did say that in my speech.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But at the same time, I think my point was that we should not keep talking ourselves down or be held back by the past.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think the Minister himself acknowledges this fact when he says that we are a Singapore Tapestry, we are not ossified.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There is a fabric of hope, he mentioned.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, would he not agree with me then that to keep this Tapestry alive, really, we have to refresh our conversations from time to time about such matters.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder what the Minister has to say about that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Last of all, perhaps, for now, I hope that the Government is not saying that its mind is closed on these matters because if they want to engage across generations who may have different aspirations, then we all need to keep an open mind and from time to time, we have to be prepared to look at things without being held back.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, I think I heard her say in her speech that some believe we may never get there as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But nonetheless, it is a process that has to constantly evolve and certainly the minds are not closed to this conversation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is why I have pitched in my speech that we must continue to have active discourse, civic participation, gain new ideas and constantly look at the problem.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To the Member's third point – whether or not there are difficulties, economic or otherwise, with the problem, it is something that we have worked into the system and into the scheme for some time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is a question of the priorities that we wish to put but also at the same time, some of these difficulties can form the conversations that we discuss – look at the trade-offs, look at the balances that we have to put in place and weave that into our discussion as to whether something ought to be changed, something ought to be tweaked.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But not at any one point in time forgetting that the overarching and overriding concerns that we have is that we must build a nation that respects each race, that each race has a place at the table and that every race must be encouraged to and indeed share the common Singapore identity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Within that constraint, we can have the conversations that Ms Lim spoke about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We can look at the priorities that she spoke about and we can look at the different considerations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I want to assure Ms Lim that the minds are not closed on these issues.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Otherwise, I believe the consequences are very serious on many families who, since I have made that speech, have written to me with their own experiences of the policy affecting them and the price differentials in the sale of flats was even higher than what I had encountered before I made this speech.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, certainly as I mentioned earlier, this is something that is within the factors that we will consider.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I want to emphasise that we need to look at why we do something and the purpose and objective of the policy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Within that, I think we have acknowledged that it is an intrusive social policy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It has always been looked at as a balancing mechanism at ensuring that we do not tilt in favour of one side more so than another.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is a factor of looking at the balance rather than the individual specifics and making sure that we achieve the overall balance and objective that I outlined.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, I would like to share my aspirations for a fair and equitable society, with opportunities for all.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One that is anchored by an education system that celebrates diversity and a social support system that recognises that while we have similar ambitions, we are not all starting from the same place.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of my generation benefited from the broad-based social uplift that began post-independence.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our lives improved and we experienced first-hand Singapore's journey from third world to first.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We know and believe that the Singapore story has been one of opportunity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I entered the field of social work when I entered university because of my passion to help families improve their lives and enable children to do better than their parents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the years, I have seen families with multiple and complex problems – drug addictions, divorce, domestic violence, children dropping out of school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I have seen how these and many other problems adversely affected them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Yet, with the right support and motivation, I have also seen how they overcame the odds and emerged stronger.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We had to spend more time and resources to support and to work with them to resolve their problems.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But it was all worthwhile to see how their lives transformed.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But there are also families where the problems appear entrenched, sometimes spanning generations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am sure Members of the House would have met some of them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For these families, we need to support them better and sometimes differently – to walk that journey at a suitable pace and give them hope at every step of the way towards a better future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I have sometimes asked myself, as many in the House have – what more can we do to help these families?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Does our support come with too many strings attached that they retreat and do not want to seek help?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Are the requirements we ask of them set too high?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed we must continue to seek ways to uplift our families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On reflection, I believe that there are two crucial ingredients required for families to seize opportunities and progress.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we must not undermine the importance of self-determination – the belief in the possibility of a brighter future and the willingness to put in the hard work that is needed to get there.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is the spirit of our Pioneer Generation that I have seen embodied in many of the families that I have worked with.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is the spirit that my father had taught me and the one that I pass on to my children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But at the same time, we know the challenges that these families face can be significant, complex and overwhelming.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must provide an environment that enables and empowers them, and gives them hope and opportunities to succeed.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our systems and structures need to support this.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking back at the last few decades, many will agree that Singapore has done fairly well to ensure broad-based opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have seen the results – more have moved up and experienced middle-class standards.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has increased to well over 90% today.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The increases in income and education are not only substantial but also substantive – they enable people to have more choices and resources to chart their own future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is higher than in other developed countries like the US and Denmark.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Yet as much as we want our citizens to progress together, for some, the path takes longer and is more complex to navigate.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The issue is how wide the gap is.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Like many cities, our inequality has been relatively high, but we have put in place a progressive system of taxes and transfers to moderate it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have kept our tax burden on our lower and middle income low, while providing support to ensure that they can access basic goods like housing, healthcare and education.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a challenge faced by many advanced countries, not just Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many in this House have spoken about this topic.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Unlike in Singapore’s early years, where most of us were from humble backgrounds, over time, we have done well, and many have been able to pass on the advantages to their children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is understandable, as we all want the best for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But across generations, those at the bottom will face increasingly unequal starting blocks.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has been exacerbated by globalisation and digitalisation, which while presenting new economic opportunities, may also worsen wage dispersion, disrupt existing occupations and threaten to leave behind those who are unable to cope in the new economy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, we need to monitor, review and adapt our policies, wherever needed, to ensure that they continue to serve our needs well, and that we continue to provide the right environment for families to seize opportunities and move up in life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we must continue to invest in the fundamentals.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need to ensure that all Singaporeans, regardless of income, can continue to meet their basic needs, and achieve a reasonable standard of living.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These mean different things to different people – what is a necessity for one, may be a good-to-have for another.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over time, these standards – on education, healthcare, housing, transport, food – will continue to change, and our expectations of them will change too.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And because there are different definitions of what is "basic" or "reasonable", expectations on what the Government and the community should provide also differ.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite these differences in views and changes in expectations, it is important that we agree on the fundamentals of our social compact, and I believe we can.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These include: for our young children, it is about giving them an education that will develop their character and prepare them well as adults and lifelong learners; for our youth, that they can advance through a vibrant job market and pursue their passions; for the young couples, that they can have a home to call their own and affordably raise a family; for our adults, that they can have job security and prepare sufficiently for their retirement; for our seniors, that they can grow old with their loved ones beside them and with dignity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to ensure that these are achievable goals for all Singaporeans, regardless of their background.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That is why we invest heavily in education at all levels for all Singaporeans and we set aside more resources for those from low-income families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recently enhanced bursaries for our full-time diploma and undergraduate students.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our investments extend beyond school, to encourage lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through the SkillsFuture movement, we support our workers to re-skill and up-skill, so that they can find good jobs and seize opportunities in growth sectors in the economy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But even as we continue to invest in these fundamentals, our conversations on the kind of social compact we want must continue.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There needs to be societal consensus on what is a basic and reasonable standard of living that we commit to provide to all Singaporeans, bearing in mind that increases in support and benefits provided are not free, but ultimately paid for by everyone through taxes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must remain committed to the fundamental aim of Singapore being a place where our efforts are rewarded not just in economic terms, but in the quality of life we enjoy; and a society where everyone has a place that is valued equally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, to achieve greater social mobility and reduce inequality in a sustainable way, we need to ensure progress for all.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Relative social mobility is important, but by itself, and its focus on comparison, it is always a zero-sum game, where a step forward for one is a step backwards for another.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We fail to see that both can actually still be doing well and better in their own ways.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indeed, for mobility to be meaningful, we also need absolute mobility – a system where everyone is progressing together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Senior Minister Tharman has likened this to a moving escalator.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If the escalator is moving up, being overtaken by someone matters less.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The differences between each step is less stark because overall, our lives are still improving.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Even as we deal with the COVID-19 crisis, we must press on with our long-term commitment to build a strong and dynamic economy that can give our workers good jobs, reasonable wages, and sustained wage increases with commensurate increase in productivity and skills.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we may have to accept that rapid growth may be more difficult, as our society matures.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For those that grew up in the 1950s, 1960s, 1970s – like me – we started from a low base.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We saw significant improvements in our lives and made a quantum leap in a generation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are now at a much higher base, and we may not be able to replicate the same quantum leap of improvements.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Steady progress is still possible if we continue to invest in creating good jobs for our people and supporting our industries to transform and remain relevant to the world.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has taken on greater urgency given the unprecedented challenges posed by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this new phase of development, can Singaporeans’ aspirations continue to be met?

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My view is that our well-being and success should not be defined solely by the academic qualifications that we possess, or how much money we earn, or how big our house is, or what kind of car that we drive.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is something we must define for ourselves.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And we know this must evolve with successive generations based on the circumstances they grow up in.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, while we cannot ensure equal outcomes, we must strive for greater equality of opportunity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is not just about access to education, health, and other public goods, which I spoke about earlier.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But rather, that our starting point in life should not dictate our ending point, and that with hard work, ability, and ambition, we can succeed.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must strive as much as possible to level uneven starting blocks, and to provide opportunities at every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE has made significant moves in recent years to address this, and in the years ahead, we will continue to do more, to give all our students opportunities to excel.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we have broadened our definition of merit – to go beyond grades and paper qualifications, to skills and ability – to allow more to access opportunities in society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have made major changes across our education system – our PSLE scoring system, how we admit students into schools and institutes of higher learning – to recognise the diverse skills and talents of our students.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also providing multiple pathways and opportunities to cater to our students’ different learning styles, abilities, and interests, and to allow them to pursue their diverse aspirations and achieve their fullest potential.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A key part of this is our efforts to move beyond streaming, to full subject-based banding.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also been enhancing porosity and creating more pathways to the higher education sector.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, through the expansion of aptitude-based admissions, including for working adults.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also creating more pathways for young Singaporeans, including Polytechnic graduates, to take up a publicly-funded degree.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the years, the increase in our CPR has benefited Polytechnic graduates.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All this is also in the spirit of the SkillsFuture movement, which represents a continuous and broad meritocracy where people can continue to learn and access new opportunities throughout life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But, fundamentally, for real change to be felt, society must be ready to accept and act on broader definitions of merit.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has to be reflected in our personal choices: as students, choosing an educational path not because it is the most popular, but because it is aligned with our interests and passions; as parents, giving our children the encouragement and space to do so; and as employers, in the way we hire and recognise our workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, on top of expanding opportunities and broadening merit throughout life, at MOE, we are investing additional resources and effort to uplift the disadvantaged and help them benefit from these opportunities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are enhancing access to quality and affordable pre-school education, to temper inequalities from the start, and lay a strong foundation for every child.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Children from low-income families also receive upstream support through programmes like KidSTART, which supports parents in areas such as health, social and child development.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To ensure that every child can develop to their full potential, we provide more manpower, including teachers, and funding to schools with greater needs, to allow them to provide effective targeted interventions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These include programmes to support academically weaker students, as well as priority access to after-school care and subsidies for student care fees for those from disadvantaged families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of these programmes, such as literacy and numeracy support programmes, are conducted in smaller pull-out classes of eight to ten students, to provide more focused support for lower progress students.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For students with special educational needs, we ensure that they are supported – whether they study in our mainstream schools, where they are supported by teachers trained in special needs and Allied Educators in Learning and Behavioural Support; or in our Government-funded Special Education schools, which are a more customised learning environment where they can thrive.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we are thinking hard about how to transform the way our programmes are delivered, to ensure that we can better journey alongside those that need help, so that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One example is UPLIFT – or the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through UPLIFT, we are looking at the unique circumstances of such students and their families, and ensuring that they get the help that they need.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we are going upstream, to strengthen support to those who show early signs of emerging issues such as irregular attendance in school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By identifying and addressing their needs early, we can build in protective factors and provide sustainable support to prevent their situation from deteriorating further.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we are strengthening partnerships across Government, and with the community, to provide wrap-around support for disadvantaged students and their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One key initiative is the UPLIFT Community Pilot, where an UPLIFT Town-Level Coordinator works closely with disadvantaged students and their families to link them up to local community programmes and resources, such as social workers and social service agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also explore expanding UPLIFT efforts to the Polytechnics and ITE students.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, the question is the kind of society that we want to be collectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just last week, I asked a few youths in my constituency about what a fair and equal society meant to them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of them told me that she had felt looked down upon when her schoolmates found out that she was receiving financial assistance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Another shared that he felt an invisible divide between himself and some of his other University mates, because he had come from a so called "less prestigious" school.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both of them were passionate about their desire to change society, so that others would not have to feel the same way as they did.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This conversation left me somewhat unsettled, about how material divides can translate to social divides, yet still reassured by the drive of our youths to better society and make a difference.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ensuring opportunities in society cannot just be about systems and structures.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is also about the values that shape our actions and define us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These values are both organic, and carefully nurtured.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Education has always played a critical role in the latter.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through our Character and Citizenship Education or CCE curriculum, we strive to instil in our students a strong sense of values and purpose, so that they can prepare for a dynamic future, where issues of diversity and inclusiveness may increasingly come to the fore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These values cannot be just learned within school, but also applied in life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have revamped the CCE curriculum to go beyond the classroom.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We strive to have our students internalise values into their hearts and not just in their minds.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that as they go out and clean our beaches, they will come home and contribute to ensuring the cleanliness of their own neighbourhoods; or as they spend time in senior homes, that they will come home and connect with the lonely elderly in their own neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to encourage our students to engage in deeper conversations about topics such as equality and inclusivity, to relate these to real-life issues, and take concrete steps to address them and put their values into action.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is really the heart of our education system.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we must not confuse this with being blind to the genuine differences and contexts across races, neither should we ignore or underestimate the severe and sometimes unintended negative consequences that can easily occur with unrestrained comments on race relations and related issues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is in this spirit of respect for all races, social cohesion, nationhood, and togetherness, that I want to reiterate several fundamental principles that I hope we will continue to agree on.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, to be an inclusive society, we must accept that there are differences across races, and approach these differences constructively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These could be differences in cultural traditions and practices, emphasis on priorities and what matters more in life, but also the specific community problems or issues that members of a race group find that they have to grapple with, that require dedicated attention and assistance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: An inclusive Singapore must recognise, appreciate, understand and accommodate these differences, and allow this positive sense of racial identity to exist and develop, and have a comprehensive set of policies and community initiatives, including self-help groups, to address issues and be part of a larger ecosystem that provides help and solves problems effectively and with empathy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To be truly Singaporean does not at all mean that we must forgo or dilute our racial identity, or pretend that we are not of a particular race, or cannot see the race of a fellow Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need to be aware and respect differences.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This common attitude has contributed to the richness of Singapore’s culture, and did not mask the race groups as if races and their differences do not exist.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our policies, practices and public discussions must avoid playing up misunderstanding ethnic differences, as well as not deny and mask genuine differences.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The underlying value and guiding principle must be mutual respect for differences and strengthening social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And I believe I speak for many in my Malay community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are proud of our rich Malay culture and heritage and beautiful Malay language.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Now, allow me to speak in my Malay language.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Speaker, to build a fairer and equal more equitable society requires everyone to play a part.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from the Government, our communities also play a key role.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will now discuss three areas that we will require to strengthen our Community's Core.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is because our Muslim community lived harmoniously with other communities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Other foreign visitors have marvelled at the modern facilities that they saw in our mosques and at Muis, a statutory board, to oversee the religious needs and development of the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What we have here is not always the case in other countries, where there are cultural rifts between races, where minorities may be marginalised, and often times, socioeconomic opportunities and the aspiration to succeed differs with other communities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a result of over 55 years of painstaking effort and belief in the common desired outcome of racial and religious harmony, supported by policies that may not be popular but necessary.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Every community understands the importance of placing this above their individual needs and are prepared to make adjustments and at times, sacrifices.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our Malay/Muslim community has also played its part.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have been committed to building a Community of Success, forging a progressive identity in a plural and contemporary Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Like all other religious groups, Muslims are free to practice their religious beliefs and customs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, maintaining our racial and religious harmony requires continuous effort on all fronts and by every community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need to adapt quickly to evolving issues and challenges as we maintain harmony.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Interfaith and inter racial relations, are dynamic and evolve over time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These relations can be influenced by regional and global trends, creating fault lines.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These fault lines can easily be exploited by internal and external elements, if we are not cautious or careful.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To help our community navigate such issues, Muis envisioned the Singapore Muslim Identity, which details the 10 desired attributes of Singaporean Muslims.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This vision and its attributes have guided us, a minority Muslim community in a multicultural society, encouraging us to be progressive, adaptive and inclusive in our religious life and live harmoniously in Singapore’s multiracial and multireligious society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Living together can sometimes give rise to disagreements, despite our best intentions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must manage these difficult conversations sensitively, via constructive dialogue on our differences while preserving the social cohesion that binds us together as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need a strong religious leadership core, who can help the Malay/Muslim community navigate these sensitive issues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This enables them to lead and guide competently and confidently.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, our asatizah demonstrated their optimistic and progressive attitude during this COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The advent of COVID-19 meant that we could no longer go to the mosque or attend face-to-face religious classes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some of our younger asatizah, particularly in the Asatizah Youth Network, had already been doing extensive engagements on social media.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The rest of our much older asatizah were quick to upgrade themselves and pick up new digital skills, so that they could conduct online sermons and classes, to ensure continuous access to religious content for our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Even though these were difficult decisions, and I am grateful that our religious leadership took early and decisive action.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The essence of leadership is the ability to make sound and well-considered decisions, even if they are unpopular and are difficult to be accepted by some segments of the community, but should be done in the interest of the larger community and society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our asatizah made these decisions as they understood the context of virus transmission in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also aware that religious authorities in other countries, made the similar decisions, in the months that followed.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, our future asatizah will face unprecedented dilemmas and challenges, and they need to be ready to equip themselves with knowledge in new areas, as well as adopt new methods in providing leadership and guidance to members of the community, in a fast-changing and uncertain world.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, our efforts to help the vulnerable to achieve their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our community has done well over the past decades.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, there are still those who are saddled with multiple social challenges – impacting adversely on their children’s growth and potential.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through UPLIFT, we will approach children who show early signs of emerging issues, such as irregular attendance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also strengthen partnerships across Government, and with the community, to mobilise energy and resources and provide comprehensive support for students and their families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have worked hard to take care of their basic needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Often, they are unable to contemplate longer-term issues, such as education, upskilling and financial planning.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They live from paycheck to paycheck, and COVID-19 has only made their situation more complex and challenging.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am often told about their dilemma – many are self-employed and do food deliveries.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I was told that if they work hard, they can earn as much as $2,500 a month, in cash.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Their hours are long, from morning until late at night.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, they are actually at a disadvantage and lose a lot of benefits, compared to those who take on permanent employment – such as employer's CPF contribution (17%), paid leave (at least 14 days), hospitalization leave (60 days), and better career opportunities, but with a lower take-home pay.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The main issue is that if they do not work, there is no pay, for instance, if they fall ill.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The risk is high to themselves, their family and their own finances.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a real trade-off for the family – whether they can pay the bills, or support their children’s education and other longer-term needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I understand these trade-offs are never easy for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Yet I worry if these families continue with this trajectory.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But if we rally together as a community, we can help relieve some of these pressures for fellow members of our community and citizens; to stabilise them and work together to chart a brighter future for their children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The third aspect that we need to strengthen is our spirit of self-help, with strong institutions like M3 (Mendaki, MUIS, and Mesra) and other Malay/Muslim organisations serving the community – particularly helping to uplift vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under the M3 initiative, the Bersamamu programme supports soon-to-wed and newly-wed couples to start strong families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Community volunteers act as "marital first responders" to provide basic marriage advice to vulnerable Malay/Muslim couples.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With a more comprehensive wrap-around care, these couples will have early access to guidance and support as they meet various challenges.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also ensure our community has access to available opportunities to improve their employability.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus, to complement the national SkillsFuture movement, the community set up the SG Teguh Bersatu Taskforce, to support those affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Taskforce which comprises Mendaki SENSE, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI), and other Malay/Muslim Organisations, as well as NTUC, aim to encourage our community to reskill and upskill to enhance their employability, build resilience and provide assistance to the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: KURNIA@WGS is yet another initiative that demonstrates the strength of our community – with eight Malay/Muslim organisations working hand in hand to help families seeking help at WGS via a one stop centre concept.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has been tough on many within our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: People are losing their jobs and the economy is increasingly bleak.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we quickly banded together to as a community to mobilise our resources to help one another.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Muis received over 7,700 applications throughout the application period.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Taken together, these efforts demonstrate the strength of the Singapore Malay community in being self-reliant, while working together with the perseverance of every member of the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through this, we grow stronger as a Community of Success – one that is adaptable and stands united in overcoming any challenges, while contributing to the common good of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is the impact when we are self-reliant – we are able to find solutions to problems and challenges we face while contributing to the development of the nation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These efforts exemplify the spirit of the Singapore Together movement, where Singaporeans partner with the Government, to own, shape and act on our shared future together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, now let me conclude in English.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I started my speech by talking about how the Singapore story has been one of opportunity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It has allowed many of us from humble beginnings to not only do well today but also do good to uplift others.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But like many advanced societies, inequality and social mobility is a challenge and the path ahead will not be an easy one.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The crux of this is harnessing the diversity on which Singapore has been built, and how we have thrived all these years.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This diversity has enabled us to not only be competitive in the world, but also colourful as a nation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: First, let me say that I appreciate where Minister Maliki is coming from.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In fact, we are of the same age.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I think we do understand each other to a large extent.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: To clarify, he earlier mentioned that we should approach society's future with boldness.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And certainly, I think all of us celebrate the ethnic diversity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: At the same time, with such a national body, there will be the advantage of pooling of national resources from the whole population that will be contributing to this pool.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And it will also have the additional uplifting effect for some that they are actually contributing to a race-blind fund.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I wanted to ask whether he thinks that this discussion can be opened, and I think will be interesting to find out whether Singaporeans prefer to contribute monthly to a race-blind fund or to contribute monthly to a community-based fund.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Indeed, we are in the same age group, born in the same year, and went through similar experiences, I guess.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Because of the success of MENDAKI and ability for us to reach out to the Malay community together with support from the Government, SINDA and CDAC were formed.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Today, I am sure Ms Sylvia Lim also knows that we do not work in silos.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Over the years, we have made efforts to work together.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But while we work together in different platforms, we also recognise that the uniqueness of each self-help group does serve our respective community better to a certain extent.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is what we often talk about – unity in diversity – and I think we should continue to celebrate this diversity.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For many, many years, I have worked with SINDA; I have worked with CDAC.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But I think my personal belief is that we should continue along this line, and where possible, where we can galvanise our resources together, we can do that.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But backend, MENDAKI, SINDA and CDAC will then proceed with the necessary administrative processes that they have put in place.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, there are already efforts at collaboration, and I think it has worked well, and I think is useful for Ms Sylvia Lim to also perhaps get further feedback from the other self-help groups, and I think we should continue to allow this diversity, to continue in the way we have managed issues faced by the respective communities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Certainly, I would be most keen to take feedback from all groups available.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I certainly hope, in the same vein and more importantly, that the Government will also have a sensing with Singaporeans, and particularly the younger generation, whether this is the model that they want to continue forever.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I want to assure Ms Sylvia Lim that we have been talking to the younger generations for the many years we have been in politics and even before that.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Those in the younger generation do also grow up, and when they grow up, sometimes their perspective change too.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Today, we will continue to talk to our younger generation.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We have the MENDAKI Club, which is the younger generation of young Malay activists; CDAC has their younger Chinese activist club, and so does SINDA.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think each of our communities do talk to each other; each of the members of the young communities in MENDAKI Club, CDAC as well as SINDA will continue to talk and engage in conversations.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And I think we remain open to look at what evolves.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: My point is that as we talk about all this amalgamation as suggested by Ms Sylvia Lim, we do have to also look at the uniqueness of this cultural nuances that is very necessary, sometimes, to find those solutions required for the respective communities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just one point of clarification to the hon Minister, Mr Maliki Osman.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: He spoke about the continued relevance in the eyes of the Government of the CMIO framework that we are members of different ethnic groups in terms of how we are viewed by Government systems and processes and so on, and that it is important to keep that in mind.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Over time we have seen more and more interracial marriages between Singaporeans of different ethnic groups.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Government has more recently allowed double-barrelled ethnic classification on the NRIC.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think that has become a process that has gained some momentum.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: As time goes by, we may even find more marriages between a Singaporean from an interracial marriage and another Singaporean from an interracial marriage.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, I do not think it is an issue as to how the children should identify themselves.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: When I come across mixed marriages, both parents are equally proud to want their children to grow up in the respective cultures.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have heard from what he said that there are few things that we have to take note of and cultivate in a person in education, like in character, moral values, intercultural interactions and also lifelong learning.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think the important thing is while we have all these ideals and objectives that we want to achieve, what are the supporting changes that we are going to make to the curriculum, the delivery, the assessment and the pathways.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Of course, I think the Minister has covered some of them.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If you can share more on those, I would appreciate very much.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think I would encourage Mr Leong to raise this at another platform because I think this is not the right forum to elaborate on what the Ministry is doing.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But suffice to say that I have shared in my speech that we are looking at education beyond just the academic.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: About character building, I have elaborated quite significantly on Citizenship and Character Education.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
