text: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act and the new rental relief framework for SMEs have been beneficial and provided some peace of mind for our entrepreneurs.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, it is temporary and the hard reality kicks in after the COVID-19 measures are lifted.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some businesses may want to restart but they have a problem of getting fresh credit.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many also worry about their old debts having snowballed.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the case of rental arrears, these businesses must now cope with repayments due under the rental relief on top of their already strained cashflow situation.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This can be patterned along the lines of the COVID-19 re-payment scheme for rent arrears.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These additional moves would provide entrepreneurs more runway to pay their debts, ensuring their mental wellness while attempting to restart their businesses.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Fourth, more innovation can take place when companies look beyond its specific vertical and sector.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Cross sectoral collaborations provide opportunities where skillsets can be combined synergistically to create new business products and services.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To enable more of such cross-industry collaborations, we need to add horizontal layers in our current way of structuring industry verticals.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Government officers will need to have horizontal exposure and skill sets to better support our companies.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We will need to promote more networking opportunities and collaborations between trade associations.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We need to promote more Joint Venture opportunities.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Let us keep finding more ways to integrate all our efforts further so  that there is more collaboration between partners so that we achieve higher network effect for our enterprises.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: COVID-19 brought structural imbalances of the landlord-tenant relationship to bare.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For many SMEs who are tenants, they rely on an equitable partnership with their landlords to thrive.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Those who are fortunate to have landlords who adopt a partnership mindset have a higher chance to thrive and as they grow, their landlords benefit too as they take up more space.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As with all types of relationships, there needs to be trust and trust is built on transparency.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We need to ensure a fair and transparent relationship between landlords and tenants so that both can grow in a sustainable manner with the end goal of providing societal well-being.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In a nutshell, we need to: (a) view our Singapore enterprises as having both economic and societal value.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As such, we need to broaden and recalibrate our performance indicators when supporting them; (b) we need to enhance our existing grant schemes to enable our entrepreneurs and their enterprises to revive, rejuvenate and re-start; (c) we need to provide an assured legal framework on insolvency and debts repayment for targeted companies and entrepreneurs to enable them to restart now and after COVID-19; (d) we need to develop an eco-system to enable more cross sector collaborations; and (e) through a Fair Tenancy Framework, provide a conducive and fair environment for our SMEs to thrive in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First off, I would like to thank all Singaporeans for the opportunity to be part of the team entrusted with the responsibility to help steer Singapore and Singaporeans through COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is unquestionably the worst crisis in a generation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have had to strike a fine and delicate balance between protecting Singaporean lives and preserving their livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This pandemic has presented an unprecedented threat to our society and economy, as it has been more virulent and widespread than any other outbreak that we have dealt with in the past.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As such, we have had to constantly calibrate our responses based on the evolving global and local situation, and the attendant risks and complexities of the various scenarios.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One very good example is the whole-of-Government effort to manage the COVID-19 outbreak in our migrant worker dormitories.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In early April, we convened a Joint Task Force comprising officers from MOM, MOH, MCI, SAF, the Home Team and other agencies, to provide support to migrant workers and dormitory operators in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now, we are transitioning towards a more sustainable approach of maintaining and preserving the health of our migrant workers for the longer term.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The ACE Group will continue to maintain the discipline as well as the cadence of screening, containment, isolation and active contact tracing of cases.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond that, they will also play a larger role in the assurance and engagement by ensuring safe working, safe living, and safe rest days for migrant workers, as well as reach out to at-risk workers to provide additional medical and mental health support.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To engender a strong support network for migrant workers, the ACE Group will also partner representatives from amongst the workers, the dormitory operators, employers and non-governmental organisations (NGOs).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And even as we plan ahead, we will not let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Other than the physical health, we are also focusing on the mental health and well-being of our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our Forward Assurance and Support Teams, or FAST Teams for short, work closely with NGOs, the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), MOH officers and the migrant worker community to identify and assist workers who are in need of mental health support.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also been regularly disseminating mental health materials in the native language of migrant workers, to teach them how to identify symptoms of distress, practise relaxation techniques, to look out for one another, and also provide information on how and where to seek help, if needed.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes general helplines and tele-counselling services run by NGOs, such as the Migrant Workers' Centre and HealthServe.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are also actively engaging dormitory operators and owners to make infrastructural changes to purpose-built dormitories, so as to enable our dormitories to become more resilient and to prevent new public health threats to our migrant workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, we are looking to improve ventilation and spacing of the living areas and communal facilities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The 100,000 beds, they are in more permanent structures.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These temporary structures can be constructed quickly, so that we can put in place measures soon to house workers further apart for better social distancing.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It will continue to evolve but our mission will also evolve alongside with it.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will remain ready, we will remain responsive to tackle the new challenges that COVID-19 will bring to us and we will ensure that our migrant workers and our Singaporean community continues to remain safe and healthy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Turning back to the present, our economy continues to be battered by the storm and difficult days remain ahead.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We need to strike the right balance between saving lives and saving livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is a constant daily challenge for all of us, as we methodically reopen the economy to our varied trading partners and foreign visitors, whilst ensuring that Singaporeans remain protected from successive waves of infection.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As a small country reliant on external trade, we are susceptible to rising nationalism worldwide as well as growing tensions between our major trading partners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will need to remain resilient to the very real possibility of disruptions to our global supply chains, which depend heavily on the modern-day business concepts of just-in-time delivery.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As most of you would have known, I have spent all of my working life in the private sector, so I can closely relate and resonate with what businesses are going through right now.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There is a Chinese idiom: “创业难，守业更难”, which means “to start a business is already not easy, but sustaining a business is even harder”.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, the challenges that face our businesses today are significant.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is regardless of whether you are a start-up, a small, medium enterprise (SME) or a large multi-national company (MNC).

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even in normal times, there were no past precedents or protocols that you can refer to when you get curve balls thrown at you.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And this happens frequently, sometimes, even on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Just like during this current COVID-19 crisis, one, our teams at MOM and MND, our Multi-Ministerial Task Force chaired by Minister Gan and Minister Lawrence Wong on a daily basis, they have to constantly think on their feet, to adapt and to adjust as the situation evolves, as more information comes onstream.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The only way we can stay ahead is to continually keep ourselves engaged with the situation as it evovles. 我们要随机应变。 Competition is also relentless for smaller firms.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It does not stop when you survive and become larger, because then you face even more capable competition not just locally but regionally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Those that make it to the big leagues, internationally, they then have to pit themselves against other large conglomerates with a wealth of resources and expertise to compete with you, and contend sometimes with protectionist rules and regulations in foreign jurisdictions that curtail the ability to compete in a fair and equitable manner.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To expand on the sentiment in the Chinese idiom, I would add: “创业难，守业更难! 要改革企业更是难上难!” While sustaining a business is harder than starting a business, when you finally have to pivot your business, or even an entire country's mindset, to be ready for new challenges is even more complex and is infinitely difficult.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even before COVID-19, our businesses and workers were already transforming themselves to prepare for the future economy and the future of work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This crisis has accelerated the changes to our economy and has highlighted the fact that we must be flexible, we must be nimble in pivoting to new areas of opportunity and different ways of operating even after this pandemic recedes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will not be an easy feat, but our Government will walk with workers and with our businesses to forge ahead on this path, even as we tackle the immediate challenges presented by the crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We want to walk with our workers to secure good employment outcomes for every generation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we navigate through this crisis, we must always remember that our workers are at the heart of our economy and we must help our workforce to emerge stronger from this crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I am particularly concerned about the growing concentration of disengaged Singaporeans in two key groups: one, the young graduates; and two, mature workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are working very hard to keep our young workers engaged and inspired as they embark on their journeys into the working world amidst this crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I want to assure all of our young Singaporeans that although you may seem to have been dealt with a difficult starting hand, we will do all we can to ensure that your generation will still flourish and fulfil your potential.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As an example, one such young graduate is Mr Foo Sek Eng, he is a 26-year-old who graduated from the Nanyang Technological University in July 2019 with a degree in Mechanical Engineering.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Sek Eng was looking out for suitable opportunities that would allow him to pursue his interest in technology and product management, and was attracted to the wide range of traineeships on offer.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He has since joined Singtel as a trainee in July 2020.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As part of his traineeship, Sek Eng has been applying his engineering background to address product innovation and data analytics issues.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He aims to develop a well-rounded skillset through his traineeship, honing not just his technical competencies, but also his project management, business development and interpersonal skills.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are very heartened by Sek Eng’s positive attitude and his enthusiasm in learning and growing through his traineeship opportunity.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even though it is a traineeship role, it has been a meaningful experience for him to build up industry-relevant skills, as well as networks and this will stand him in better stead to secure a good full-time job and I hope, perhaps, spur him off on this entrepreneurship journey to do a start-up in his own field of interest, especially when the economy recovers and I hope his example inspires many others in his generation, and this will give our young workers confidence that there are opportunities to flourish in spite of this crisis.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We also want to foster the grit and innovative spirit of our young entrepreneurs, whose companies will be a key part of our strong Singaporean core of enterprises that can compete internationally and offer high-end quality jobs locally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One such other enterprise is Lucence, which was founded by Dr Tan Min-Han in 2016.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He chose to set up his own company to build world-class medical technology in a very highly competitive industry.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Because he wanted to strike out on his own, he wanted to put his name and Singapore’s name on the world map, and successfully compete with global conglomerates.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In doing so, his company has achieved outside as the only US federally-licensed medical diagnostic lab in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The company has also pivoted in this COVID-19 crisis to developing a more sensitive saliva test kit using this deep-throat saliva and we are now doing studies to see how we can adapt it for use locally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This group – mature workers – is near and dear to my heart, because I am in the age group.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our mature workers in their 40s and 50s have contributed a good part of their lives to our economy so far.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Most of them continue to be willing, and they are able to contribute to our economy for many, mnay more years to come, but even before the pandemic struck, many were already concerned about their job securities and the challenges of how they can adapt to the new technology and how this new technology has transformed their job scope and their work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the current weak labour market conditions, many are worried about losing their jobs, having to compete with younger counterparts or even foreign workers for limited job opportunities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The reality is that many sectors and many jobs that have been worst-hit by this crisis may take a long time to bounce back, and some of them may never, never come back.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, these companies would have to pivot their operations or ride on new opportunities that arise.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As our mature workers strive to prepare themselves for new job roles, we must also make sure that employers consider them fairly and offer them good opportunities for improvement and progression.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Meritocracy is the foundational principle of Singapore society and we must demonstrate this to the world by taking a stand against employers that discriminate against workers based on nationality, age, gender or any other factors that are irrelevant to the job.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mature workers possess a significant treasure trove of experiential knowledge and practice wisdom.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This experiential knowledge and practice wisdom cannot be replaced by or gleaned from academic pursuits or qualifications.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Like what they say in Chinese: 姜是越老越辣 – the older the ginger, the spicier it gets.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There is significant value for companies to leverage on that expertise, and the skills sets of our mature and experienced Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I want to also reassure our businesses that we are neither inward-looking nor are we turning away global talents and investments.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to welcome those who bring in valuable skills in short supply.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Such top-tier workers allow our businesses to build the best teams in our country so that we remain globally competitive, while also helping, at the same time, to attract high-value investments and anchor high-value activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our local workers can also learn from the expertise of such skilled foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And to this end, I am glad that Mr Pritam Singh and the Workers' Party also agree and align with us on the need to support the growth of our Singapore Core, infusing it with global talent.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The two examples that Mr Singh cited with regards to MOM, these two companies amongst the 47 companies being added to the Fair Competition Framework Watchlist and asked why we had allowed them to hire as many as they did before deciding to put them on the watchlist.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And the universe that we are looking at, there are more than 35,000 companies in Singapore that hire these EPs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some of them will have problems of higher concentrations of foreigners compared to their peers, even though prima facie the EP applications have met qualifications and salary criteria.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have been stepping up the surveillance and enforcement.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, we expect businesses operating in Singapore to invest more effort in strengthening the Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the current difficult economic climate, it is all the more important that our workers are given fair opportunities to find meaningful work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And rest assured, we at MOM, not only have we been working doubly hard to monitor compliance amongst these companies, we have continued to step up surveillance and enforcement action against egregious offenders.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the long run, curtailment of work pass priviledges is not an adequate measure.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I have come from the private sector all my life.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I have run a sizeable, global conglomerate in healthcare.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I think that if we think we can choke off key manpower supply by curtailing Employment Passes or establishing a quota, I think this is going to be infinitely more painful for the companies than any other penalties that you can think of imposing.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, I would seriously and crucially advise against that kind of thinking.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also scale up our proactive efforts to increase our Singaporean jobseekers' chances of landing a suitable job.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, I would also like to make an appeal to all of our jobseekers, regardless of age and background – in this difficult economic climate, we may have to be a bit more realistic in your expectations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have to keep an open mind on the available opportunities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With support from the Government, this will give us the chance to embark on a new career path in a sector or role that some of us may not have considered before.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We also want to walk with employers, to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will also support businesses through a variety of targeted steps.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will create a more attractive environment for co-opetition, which is for businesses to compete and to also cooperate with one another for new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One recent example of this cooperation was between FormLabs, TÜV-SÜD, NUS, NUH and companies with 3D-printing capabilities, to rapidly develop swabs used in COVID-19 test kits.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They formed a consortium to leverage on digital manufacturing, and took only seven weeks to reach product readiness.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Local companies Structo, Eye2Eye, and Forefront Medical, they were involved in the conceptualisation and the entire production development cycle, and seized the opportunity to repurpose their available 3D printers to mass produce 3D-printed nasopharyngeal swabs; there was a massive run on this particular item, this is key to doing that swab in our nasopharyngeal to pick up the virus so that we can send it for PCR testing.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, there was a huge shortage in global supply due to demand surge and supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The ability of our private sector, our research institutions and our Government agencies to come together quickly to meet new needs and to seize new opportunities, puts us in good stead for co-opetition – to compete globally and also to cooperate globally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This continues to put them in the best position to seize new opportunities when the economy recovers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For businesses in industries that have permanently changed, we will help them reinvent themselves and help them pivot into new markets with new products.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many of the mass market tourism and social entertainment companies are already thinking along these lines.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, there are opportunities within these industries for Singapore to lead the way in the development of new business models that can be adopted globally.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: STB is trialling this framework with two pilot events before scaling up to other events.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, to stay ahead, Mr Speaker, Sir, it is also crucial that we develop a strong Singapore Core of enterprises that can grow and compete internationally, and offer high-end, quality job opportunities to our workforce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is not going to be an easy feat, given the fact that our domestic market is too small to sustain them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To succeed, we must find new ways to transform and innovate; not just incubate these ideas, but developing generations of Singaporeans that can put these ideas into action and commercialise them with strong intellectual property protection and validation by our Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have started to do this with business leaders through Singapore Together Alliances for Action, set up by the Emerging Stronger Taskforce.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have launched National Innovation Challenges to develop industry-led solutions to the challenges faced by businesses.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, the Safe-Reopening: Construction challenge led by BCA and Kajima Group seeks to establish a system that enables construction-site continuity planning.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will allow project development activities to resume safely and sustainably.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We must also continue to encourage partnerships with internationally renowned institutions, share and learn their best practices, and cooperate and invest to expand our talent base and our repertoire of ideas and innovations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is something I hope I can contribute to and achieve in MTI.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To conclude, we must never waste a crisis, because in every crisis, there are also opportunities : 危机—有危险就有机会。Together as a nation, we must overcome our differences in ideologies, beliefs and personalities and we must unite together in constructive feedback, in constructive engagement and we have to work together to overcome this pandemic and the pains that it has brought us.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I hope, and it is my sincere and earnest disire, that all parties can come and work together to develop a new spirit of resilience, fortitude and unity that reflects the same tenacity and grit of our forefathers.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Then, hopefully, years from now, we can look back and say that we overcomed the crisis of a generation and we have continued to live long and prosper.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To continue to do well and thrive in the brave new world, we must be exceptional.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Exceptional in the way we dream, in the way we hope, in the way we aspire, exceptional in the way we implement, in the way we execute.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Manpower and Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But most important of all, I hope that we can be exceptional in the way we care for one another and in a way we carry one another.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.39 pm until 4.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Apologies, I missed your hand earlier; must have been too hungry just now.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: This pertains to his reference to my speech and specifically the bit on fair hiring.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And reference was made there to a local IT firm found to be unfairly favouring job applicants who are foreigners.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The next line is interesting: "But it was uncooperative until six months later when a TAFEP officer received a call from their CEO".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My question pertains to the point that the Minister made in his speech about stepped-up surveillance and enforcement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can the Minister share what really this entails, going forward, in light of unfair hiring practices, how is the system going to change from what it is, what it has been?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: FCF was introduced in 2014 – it has been five over years.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is the Ministry still seeing employers who are errant and who essentially do not cooperate?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And if the Minister's approach is, "We have to engage them more", can the Minister please outline how would this be done to improve the status quo?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, we also work with these companies, with the HR directors, to see where the problem is.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Sometimes, it could be, for instance, concentration in one particular sector industry.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In other instances, it could be because of the skillsets, whether they are lacking or whether it could be the fact that Singaporeans do not want those jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That is the kind of engagement that I was alluding to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, suffice to say, today, we have stepped up, we are all working very hard to make sure that the companies work with the relevant authorities to ensure that this fair hiring, non-discriminatory type of practices is more prevalent across all the companies in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Does stepped-up surveillance and enforcement also entail increasing the budget for TAFEP, for example, or increasing manpower for surveillance purposes?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because there are thousands of these companies in Singapore and across an incredible number of industries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Together with that, with the TAFEP part, that actually takes care of the rest of the industry.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: God willing, I would certainly do my best to serve each and every constituent and to perform all my duties as their Member of Parliament in these difficult and uncertain times that our nation is facing.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Even as we are battling the crisis of a generation, it is vital that we do not lose sight of the opportunities that is before us today, and I rise today to speak of seizing the opportunities for our politics, our social safety nets, our manpower policies and our transport policies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We have been through a General Election that has many firsts in our political history.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A GE with many restrictions and additions imposed on campaigning and a polling process including the first GE without physical rallies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A deeper focus on online campaigns, a much more vocal electorate willing and able to make their voices heard online and not letting the ruling party to impose its narrative on certain election issues.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It was notable that many voters rejected gutter politics and embraced the need for a diversity of viewpoints.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The President talked about evolving politics in her speech, adding on to the discussion of good politics by her predecessor in his speech in the Opening of the Thirteenth Parliament.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Good politics must entail mutual respect between members of the ruling party and other parties, whether in Parliament or back in our constituencies.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I myself had some experience with petty and bad politics in this election, which makes me wonder whether the ruling party has gone backwards in time in the in the way its campaign had been conducted in Hougang.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: During the GE, two complaints were made to ELD about our election posters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: With respect, my experienced volunteers were puzzled as they were all very sure that they had installed the posters at the right height.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: After the first complaint, my volunteers inspected and made the necessary rectifications.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: She showed me where they allegedly took place and I have no reason to doubt what she said.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Separately in the middle of the campaign, the PAP team planted their flags in front of some of my banners, effectively blocking a clean sighting of the contents of my banners.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The PAP team also planted many flags around some of our Hougang coffee shops.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Back in 2015, I remembered I had a much different experience contesting at Fengshan SMC with the hon Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I did not have these negative experiences with Miss Chan; it was a fair and honourable fight, full credit to Miss Chan and her team.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Given what has happened, will that mean that the PAP should now also expect and allow Workers' Party to do likewise in constituencies where PAP are the incumbents?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I should think not, lest a tit-for-tat culture manifests itself and create a divisive political culture that only hurts Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Instead, we in this House have a golden opportunity to evolve our politics positively.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Even as we contest our ideas in this Chamber, we can do so in the spirit of mutual respect and understanding, knowing that even if we differ in our ideas, we are in the end One Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope the ruling party can start to accept that.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While many businesses and individuals have received assistance through the above, times are still tough for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many have lost their jobs in the last few months.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Individuals that are still employed see the slow business and fear they will lose their jobs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The self-employed, poor business conditions continue to put a strain on their financial situation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Jobseekers have difficulty securing jobs, be it the fresh graduate looking for their first job or the middle age workers seeking to find a replacement position.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many residents have sought help to appeal for assistance under the various schemes set up by the four Budgets after the GE, for example, COVID-19 grant and SIRS.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many have been doing well until early this year earning incomes as either employees or self-employed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They have also been sensible with their financial commitments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, many of them are now with considerably less income and, in some cases, zero income.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Paying for the same financial commitments becomes an issue as they dig deeper into their savings.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They get into trouble if their savings are relatively limited and selling their property may not be an option.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As a resident told me last week, unsubsidised childcare fees and even the cost of diapers and infant formula all add up to the pressure when one has no income.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While I understand the Government has drawn a line when dispensing assistance, the challenge remains as to how to help more of such people in this sandwiched class, especially if the crisis is going to go on for longer.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While efforts at retraining may be helpful in the medium or long term, many still need help to tide them over until they find new jobs.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They need the breathing room to pick themselves up to overcome the fall they have just experienced.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: (In Mandarin):   	Mr Speaker, firstly, I would like to thank the Hougang residents for giving me the opportunity to be their Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I will serve each resident to the best of my ability.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A large number of businesses and Singaporeans have received help, but many are still facing difficulties.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many have lost their jobs in recent months, and those who still have their jobs worry about losing their job due to declining business in the company they work for.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For self-employed persons, the current situation has put pressure on their finances.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Jobseekers of all levels and age groups are finding it difficult to get a job.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Many of these residents, up until early this year, had income as an employee or a self-employed person and they have also been prudent in meeting their financial commitments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: But now, many of them have seen their income dropped significantly and some even have no income at all.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If their savings could only last them for a few months, servicing their financial commitments would be a big problem.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Just as what one resident told me last week, when one has no income, the cost of unsubsidised childcare fees and even the cost of diapers and milk powder would add to their burden.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Government has set out the criteria and drawn a clear boundary when distributing assistance resources to the people.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, it remains our biggest challenge to find ways to help the sandwich class more, especially if the crisis may last for an extended period.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: From a mid- to long-term perspective, retraining Singaporeans may be helpful.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: But many of these people will still need some help to tide over the difficult time before they can land a new job.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They need a breathing space to allow them to rebound and overcome the plight that they find themselves in now.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: (In English): Sir, as retrenchment and unemployment increase, we must not be afraid to seize this opportunity to ask ourselves whether the Government should take greater steps to ensure Singaporeans are given fair share in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We have heard much anecdotal discussion online or in the coffeeshops about the notoriety of the finance or IT industry having a relatively higher number of foreign workers or how many managers have recruited people from their own countries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: By way of an example, I know a small to medium size insurance outfit with a UK Head Office and international ownership.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It has established its Asian office in Singapore more than 10 years ago, dealing with largely Singaporean and Asian customers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: From the beginning a large number of employees were expatriates from its UK Head Office who variously ran the office and took charge of various business functions such as claims in underwriting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The people who ran the office heading the various business functions here, were mid-level executives with qualifications and experiences comparable to their Singapore PMET counterparts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In my view, there is no lack of local talent in Singapore who can run this outfit and its various business functions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, the manpower situation in this company has not changed much till today.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am perplexed to learn that businesses like this can continue to operate in Singapore for such a long time without making any serious effort to have or to increase the Singaporean component at its management and senior levels.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Should we not challenge ourselves to take advantage of this opportunity to re-examine our assumptions behind employment and economic policies more holistically so as to better encourage or incentivise, or if necessary, ensure that companies make a greater effort to engage the Singaporean core at different levels of their company.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: With lighter loads on our public transport system now, there is an opportunity to review our public transport policy to better serve Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Singaporeans are highly dependent on our public transport system as we seek to build a car-lite society.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Our starting point must then be, to put our commuters first over other stakeholders and be world-class leaders in areas such as reliability, affordability and quality, a point I made before in the previous term of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, the furrow that has erupted over an announcement by LTA on planned changes to certain bus services in Bukit Panjang has illustrated the underlying tension between what the authorities perceive as prudent fiscal spending and the proper provision of public transportation to our commuters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Minister for Transport has mentioned on social media the subsidies needed for maintaining the affected MRT and bus services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We, in the Workers' Party will support Singaporeans in demanding the high standard they should expect for our public transport system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We must review the medium term vision of our public transport system.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: There is wisdom about our crisis using unique opportunities that we can seize.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We must be aware of the danger, but recognise the opportunities in this crisis so that we do not just overcome the crisis, but truly emerge a Singapore we can all be proud of.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If I heard him correctly, he mentioned of his unhappy experience in GE2020, something to do with the height of posters and the direction by the Elections Department or ELD.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He juxtaposed it with the experience in an earlier election against hon Member, Miss Cheryl Chan.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And if he accepts that, what is the basis of him suggesting that PAP would use the power of incumbency against opponents in an unfair way?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, as I said in my speech, my volunteers went to rectify it and they informed ELD that after the first complaint, the rectification had been made.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Two days later, another complaint was made to ELD and we were told about it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And this is something that I think back in 2015, I would never envisage planting Workers' Party flags around the Fengshan Block 85 market or around the coffeeshops in Fengshan.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My point really is that having seen what happened recently, if this is going to be a precedent that is going to be set by the PAP, perhaps the team in Hougang maybe, then really it raises the wider question of where do you want to draw the line with this kind of behaviour.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Because certainly for me, my own standard is, certainly as I said in 2015, I find it unthinkable that I would have gone to Fengshan and plant the Workers' Party flags around the market.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I made that point, but I think I also ended that on a different note.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I said that we have to move beyond this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: We cannot do a tit-for-tat in that sense and certainly –

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Murali was asking you about ELD and if you believe it was even-handed; and you have not quite answered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But what ELD did was, basically, it received a complaint and it asked us to go and rectify it, right?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: This is specifically referring to the incident about the poster height.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I respectfully suggest that my question still remains unanswered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: But I have raised various incidents that have happened as a result of the actions of certain people.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And my point really is that these are all very petty and bad politics, and we should not encourage it.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: They fund the lion share of our tax revenue while consuming a limited amount of Government assistance.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: As economic winners of our society, it is appropriate that they contribute to help the rest of Singapore move along.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And the majority of them have benefited from Government assistance during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Business owners and professionals benefited from Government support such as the Job Support Scheme or JSS, and corporate tax rebates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: However, a number of my private estate residents feel there it is time to review the social compact.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This group include: (a) retired seniors who are asset-rich but cash poor; (b) residents above 50 facing greater career uncertainty; (c) residents who do not own the home they stay in; and (d) residents who are deeply impacted by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: As such, I believe we should review our policies in at least three ways.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: One, the Government must create more ways to help asset rich, cash poor, private estate residents better tap on their housing equity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Of course, residents can selling their houses and downgrade.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But this will mean they are uprooted from the neighbourhoods they so cherish, especially in their golden years.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Seniors who are financially savvy can also make adequate financial planning to make sure that they can benefit from annuities and dividends.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: With the pressing economic conditions, this issue has become more urgent.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our Government can also work with our banks to remove barriers for our people to borrow against their housing equities at a feasible age, even beyond the age of 70.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I understand the banks' current reservations in lending to seniors.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Perhaps we can mandate the banks to lend against housing equity if that senior, who is Singaporean, have a Lasting Power of Attorney, so that the banks have somebody they can work with, without involving expensive legal remedies, should their clients fall ill and are mentally incapacitated.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: If our people can tap on their housing equity effectively, I believe most Singaporeans in the private estates would prefer to stand on their own two feet, instead of relying on the Government assistance.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Second, we can look at our means testing framework for those without much assets or income.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Beyond using a different yardstick, we can also consider tiering Government benefits, so as to remove the big difference of benefits between public and private housing residents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We also could review our policies on housing grants for seniors and their next generation who want to move from private housing to public estates, especially if they do not have a lot of net worth.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We can add pathways for downgrading hospitalisation ward class and therefore, cost of healthcare.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We can also review our criteria on COVID related assistance programmes such as Self-employed Person Income Relief or SIRS, and the COVID-19 Support Grant or CSG.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The Government can also communicate a clear and consistent whole-of-Government approach towards means-testing for private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Several years ago, I recall Minister Edwin Tong, in his capacity as a backbencher, giving an eloquent speech on the subject of reviewing means testing with regards to private estate residents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: During the debate, I noted that while various Ministries exercise discretions in helping specific cases, the level of discretion varies from Ministry to Ministry.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Now, it is a good time for the Government to do a thorough review and to spell out the core principles of means-testing for private estate, which can form the basis of a new social compact with our private estate residents.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Thirdly, I think there is more we can do regarding infrastructure and accessibility for private estates.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: As our seniors age, there are some estates with unique terrain that require some infrastructure upgrading.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: A good example is the Teachers' Housing Estate within my constituency, which is nested within a valley.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Many of the seniors struggle to walk up two storeys of steep stairs, just to access the bus stop.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This task force can at issues such as identifying low cost outdoor lift and escalators options to promote accessibility; promoting more power-assisted devices with shelters or roofs for seniors, and to prioritise cycling and walking paths construction in private estates with challenging terrains and a high density of seniors so that they can use PADs to get around.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Next, let me speak about strengthening the Singapore Core in our private sector.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But while much has been done, there is one particular area that I think we should also closely examine, and that is preserving and growing the base of middle and senior Singapore management and professionals, especially within international companies.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Compared to say a decade or two ago, Singapore professionals have gained significant experiences in some of the world’s most competitive areas, including areas like asset management, investment banking, management consulting, urban solutions, architecture and engineering services.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: A number of Singapore outfits, staffed by largely Singaporeans, can hold their own against the best in the world.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This includes DBS, Dymon Asia, Quantedge, Surbana Jurong, Ong and Ong Architect, Woh Hup, just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Yet, there are also many international companies that have yet to build a strong Singapore Core in their middle and senior management ranks.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In fact, as many international companies look to downsize during this pandemic, many worry that whether we will regress, rather than progress, in building our Singapore Core.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Building a Singapore Core among amongst middle and senior positions is not an easy task – I fully admit to that.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But there is urgency for us to take a fundamental relook at this approach.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And we must start by asking ourselves: are these companies making a genuine effort?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I am the first one to acknowledge the difficulty in measuring sincerity of effort.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: However, we can explore different ways of identifying tell-tail signs of systematic issues, starting with the diversity of their workforce.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: There are, of course, legitimate reasons why high paying EP jobs go to expatriates from a particular country.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: For example, an international company like Samsung, with their regional headquarters in Singapore, would likely have a high number of Koreans nationals in their management.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The IT consulting and implementation arm of Deloitte would likely have many Indian nationals because Indian IT professionals form the bulk of available IT talent in our region, and because IT capabilities are critical for our industry transformation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Also, a company from an emerging and promising industry might also need to bring in specialist talents at the start to get a new industry moving, and these talents are available in some specific countries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But short of these selected circumstances, given the talent and ability of our Singaporeans, I do not see why we cannot build up a stronger Singapore Core.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I strongly believe that majority of international and large Singapore companies are responsible and the vast majority of Singaporeans I speak to do understand the need to stay open to foreign talent even in middle and senior positions.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But we must do everything we can to call out irresponsible employers so as to maintain broad public support for manpower policy during this challenging period.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: My final point is on how we can co-create climate change policies with our people in the spirit of SG Together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: As Singapore matures as a society, our society’s definition of good governance evolves.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Talking to my residents, I get the sense that most Singaporeans think of good governance not just in terms of quality of outcome, but also in terms of transparency over process, as well as empathy and simplicity in communications.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And I believe that this Government is committed to doing exactly that.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Some time back, when Deputy Prime Minister Heng launched SG Together, he highlighted that there are many policy areas that the Government can co-create with our people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: In areas of defence and foreign policy, foreign and domestic intelligence matters, and reserve management, we must maintain confidentiality, as we are living in an increasingly dangerous world.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But in most other areas, we can do more to open up the processes, empower our people with facts, so that Singaporeans can make tough choices together.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: One particular area for co-creating with Singaporeans is climate change.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: There is this African proverb, “If you want to go fast, go alone.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: By that, I mean going beyond the occasional consultation exercise.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: It means ensuring that all stakeholders have access to the same set of core facts.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We can also regularly share how are we faring, at a programme level, not just at the whole national level, against our ambitious targets.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Having spoken to various Government officials, I am aware of the tremendous efforts and resources that our Government is pouring into this area.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I am proud to say that Singapore is one of the few countries in the world that has real political will and resources to meet our climate change obligations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Therefore, why not we share the nuts and bolts of these exciting plans, including the implementation cost and expected emissions reduction, with our people?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Despite our Government’s best efforts, however, it is likely that our current plan can only allow us to meet a bulk of our long-term emission targets.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This is where we have ample round room to co-create policy.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: I hope the Government can share the gaps openly and transparently, and then work, in the spirit of SG Together, with our environmental groups, industry, and our people to close these gaps.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This could also include putting up more calls for industrial collaboration and to elicit solid proposals from our environmental groups and our youths.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: But whatever ideas that we gather must hold up to the highest standards.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: We must make sure that these ideas are implementable and cost effective.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This outfit can assess the cost and benefit of emission reduction efforts from not just the Government, but also the proposals from the industries, environmental groups and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And also, we must also give our environmental groups, the industries and Singaporeans who have come up with these ideas the opportunity to see them through because they care.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Indeed, there are ample opportunities on how our Government bring passionate people to deliver on Government objectives.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: This includes getting our VWOs to deliver Government-funded social services, and also getting rights groups including ACRES to run the Government’s wildlife rescue service.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: If we can achieve all that, I am confident that the vast majority of Singaporeans, including our youths, will be proud of not just achieving our Climate Change obligations to the world, but also how we can do so together as one Singapore.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, Sir, I rise in support of both the long-term Government plans as outlined by the Presidential address, as well as the Motion of thanks from the hon Member Mr Patrick Tay.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Prior to the crisis, our economy was already facing immense structural challenges and shifts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Examples include an ageing population, the shift towards the gig economy and the increasing use of automation driven by Industry 4.0.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: COVID-19 has merely accelerated the pace of this transformation, at an unprecedented pace, causing our future workplace, which many had thought would happen in decades to come, to become a reality much sooner.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: All jobs and all workers will have to transform, or risk becoming obsolete.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In recent years, much of the work traditionally done by accountants, lawyers and even doctors have been automated and accomplished with greater accuracy.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Real estate agents and financial planners are already starting to be phased out by digital apps.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But are our companies, our workers and the Government ready?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In my view, it will be smarter, leaner and more connected.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the manufacturing sector, artificial intelligence and automation will mean that mundane jobs will be phased out.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As technology redefines existing job roles into smaller tasks, more jobs will be increasingly taken over by robots.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As Minister Ong Ye Kung once aptly put it, “If you work like a robot, you will be replaced by a robot”.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Our workers of tomorrow will need to learn the latest technologies and be able to work with them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One example is how autonomous vehicles (AV) will drastically redefine our land transport industry.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Since 2016, I have been highlighting in this House the impact of autonomous technology on the livelihoods of our transport workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Every year, we get closer to this reality.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am glad to see that some forward-looking companies are already taking steps to gear up their workforce for the future.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The bank, which was one of the first to embrace digital banking, has also invested significantly in its digital learning tools to enable their employees to upgrade their skills and acquire new knowledge, even while they work from home.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While big companies like DBS have the resources to plan for the future, our small and medium enterprises or SMEs are faced with a different reality.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The impact of COVID-19 on SMEs has been more pronounced and many SMEs are currently operating in the survival mode.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some are so focused on their day-to-day business that they neglect to plan for tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I urge the Government to do more to support our SMEs in adopting technology and at the same time upskilling their workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We would also need to move upstream to prepare our future workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am not suggesting that we train every Singaporean child to be a coder or an IT expert, but to understand computers and to be able to work with robots in the future workplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Countries, such as Japan, South Korea and the UK, have already taken steps in this direction, with coding and programming incorporated into the mandatory education for students.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The low latency provided by 5G technology means that working from home will become the default and remote working possibilities are endless.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Competition for jobs will truly become globalised, blurring the divide between local and foreign workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, while I welcome the recent announcement by MOM to further adjust the Employment Pass and S Pass qualifying salaries, my question is: will our work pass and Employment Pass system continue to be relevant when companies no longer need employees to be physically based in one location to perform the work?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can Singapore continue to compete for investments and bring in the best companies?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can Singaporeans continue to compete for good jobs?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As Mdm President noted in her Address, we will need to be more resilient and more nimble than others when responding to change in order to thrive in this global world.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But how can we better support our fellow Singaporeans to compete in this new world, especially when they are already facing many challenges?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: PMETs, particularly in their 40s and 50s, tell me that it is not easy to juggle between the many responsibilities that they must shoulder every day – looking after their young children, managing the healthcare needs of their elderly parents and trying to set aside funds for their own retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With this overwhelming "sandwiched" feeling, many are unable to think beyond their daily struggles.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that the Government will recognise this and look into how we can better support and alleviate these burdens.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But can we tap on technology to make our future workplace safer and healthier?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With technology, dangerous work at the worksite can be done remotely, in a safe and comfortable location.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Smart PPEs and wearable technologies will also reduce fatalities and the severity of injuries if an accident happens.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And I hope that the Government can accelerate the implementation of these technologies at our worksites, starting with the high-risk sectors such as construction and manufacturing.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As we improve workplace safety, we must not neglect workplace health.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: These past six months have taught us that blurring the lines between home and office has its challenges.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Similar laws have been implemented in other countries like Italy and the Philippines.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
